Anna —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our chat, I pulled together three straightforward advance-commit options that are tailored for early-stage startups that need predictable spend but also runway flexibility. The attached pricing grid summarizes per-token economics, term discounts, and the credit grants. High level:

- Option 1 — 12 months: $60,000 prepay, 10% term discount, $10,000 usage credits, standard monthly minimums.
- Option 2 — 18 months: $90,000 prepay, 15% term discount, $20,000 usage credits, ramped minimums (months 1–3 lower).
- Option 3 — 24 months: $120,000 prepay, 20% term discount, $30,000 usage credits, lowest unit price.

Notes on credits and rollover: credits apply to token usage and priority capacity; unused credits can be rolled into following quarter within the same term in Options 2 and 3 (we can make an exception for startups in Option 2).

Two quick questions so I can draft a clean SOW:
1) Do you have a preferred term (12/18/24)?
2) Will procurement need a PO or do you prefer DocuSign to sign the SOW?

I attached BrightLoop_Pricing_Grid_v2.xlsx with the detailed math and a draft SOW that I can redline once you confirm the option.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call to walk through.

— Soojin

- Can Option 2 be structured so months 1–3 have a lower committed minimum (we were hoping for 20–30% of the monthly average) while still preserving the aggregate prepay?

- Early termination: what protections do you offer if our needs materially change?

Procurement will likely route things through our finance team (finance@brightloop.ai) and they tend to ask for a PO-first approach.

Would welcome a quick call tomorrow to iterate.

Anna —

Thanks for the candor. Based on your constraints I sketched three revised, practical structures (short bullets + clear tradeoffs) so your finance team can pick what lines up with runway and risk appetite:

Option A — 12 months (smaller cash hit)
- $60k prepay, 10% term discount
- $10k usage credits (priority capacity)
- Standard min: 60% of average in months 1–3
- Good if you prefer minimal contract duration and quicker exit

Option B — 18 months (recommended middle ground)
- $90k prepay, 15% term discount
- $20k usage credits
- Ramped minimums: months 1–3 at 30% of the eventual monthly baseline, months 4–6 at 60%, then full pace
- Credits roll for up to one quarter if underused; can be applied to purchase additional burst capacity

Option C — 24 months (best unit economics)
- $120k prepay, 20% term discount
- $30k usage credits
- Lowest per-token price; flexible rollover of credits for half the term

On refunds: our standard is service credits rather than cash refunds. For seed-stage customers we can make a one-time carve-out to allow a partial refund (cap applies) if usage is < 15% of forecast after month 6 — would require exec approval.

I've attached a revised SOW and updated pricing grid. If procurement prefers a PO-first workflow we can accept that; otherwise I can send a DocuSign with redlines for legal. If it helps, I can put Marcus and Monica on the next call for quick approvals and legal touchpoints.

Available slots today 3–5pm PT or tomorrow morning. Which works?

— Soojin

Subject: RE: Advance commitment options for BrightLoop — internal note

Team —

I reviewed the options. For seed / pre-series-A startups I want to be flexible while protecting revenue economics. My recommended play: move forward with Option B (18 months) but with these internal concessions we can offer to secure the deal quickly:

- Make months 1–3 minimums 30% (as proposed).
- Add a one-off 3-month runway credit (applies to capacity) that acts as a buffer for initial experimentation.
- Unused credits: convert to service credits for the remaining term; allow a single partial cash refund up to 10% of credits if usage < 10% after month 6 (exec approval required).
- Include a startup-friendly clause: if BrightLoop raises a priced round and increases usage materially, we’ll offer a one-time acceleration credit to offset their next renewal.

Financial math: with the above, the effective discount for us is ~12% vs. list; acceptable given the likely expansion motion and referenceability.

Monica — please prep the SOW redline with the refund cap and the ramp minimum language. Evelyn — flag any SLA exceptions we should be comfortable with here.

Marcus
